relevance_reason: Comprehensive mutation screening of NR3C2 (MR) in renal PHA1 patients, finding MR mutations as the principal cause; also notes possible genetic heterogeneity.

findings.statement: Pujo et al. (2007) carried out a comprehensive screen of the mineralocorticoid receptor gene (MR; NR3C2) in patients with PHA1. They searched coding regions, intron-exon junctions, and untranslated exons for nucleotide substitutions and also looked for large deletions. They found 22 MR gene abnormalities in 33 patients. The authors concluded that MR mutations are extremely frequent in PHA1 patients classified according to aldosterone and potassium levels.
quotes: We present the first comprehensive study seeking nucleotide substitutions in coding regions, intron-exon junctions, and untranslated exons, as well as for large deletions.
A total of 22 MR gene abnormalities were found in 33 patients.
We demonstrate that MR mutations are extremely frequent in PHA1 patients classified according to aldosterone and potassium levels

findings.statement: Pujo et al. (2007) suggested that a genocopy may exist in 3 PHA1 kindreds that had no MR mutation. They proposed that other patients without MR mutations might have different diseases that resemble PHA1 in the neonatal period.
quotes: In our study the possibility of a genocopy exists in three PHA1 kindreds.
The other patients without MR mutations might have different diseases resembling to PHA1 in the neonatal period, which could be identified by extensive clinical and functional exploration.

findings.statement: Pujo et al. (2007) described type 1 pseudohypoaldosteronism (PHA1) as a primary form of mineralocorticoid resistance. In the newborn it presents with salt wasting, hyperkalemia, and failure to thrive. Inactivating mutations in MR (NR3C2) cause the autosomal dominant form and some sporadic cases.
quotes: Type 1 pseudohypoaldosteronism (PHA1) is a primary form of mineralocorticoid resistance characterized in the newborn by salt wasting, hyperkalemia, and failure to thrive.
Inactivating mutations of the mineralocorticoid receptor (MR; NR3C2) are responsible for autosomal dominant and some sporadic cases of PHA1.

relevance_reason: Reports NR3C2 mutations in six patients with autosomal dominant PHA1 and functional characterization of the mutants.

findings.statement: Riepe et al. (2006) identified 6 different heterozygous NR3C2 mutations in 6 patients with PHA1: a previously reported frameshift mutation (c.1131dupT), a second frameshift (c.2871dupC), 2 novel nonsense mutations generating a truncated receptor protein, and 2 missense mutations (S818L and E972G). The authors concluded that the data extended the spectrum of PHA1-causing NR3C2 mutations.
quotes: Six heterozygous NR3C2 mutations were detected. One frameshift mutation (c.1131dupT) has been reported previously.
Two novel nonsense mutations generate a truncated receptor protein. Two missense mutations differently affect MR function.

findings.statement: Riepe et al. (2006) found that the NR3C2 frameshift mutation c.2871dupC, identified in heterozygous state in a PHA1 patient, showed no aldosterone binding and no transactivation because of a major change in receptor conformation.
quotes: The second frameshift mutation (c.2871dupC), which has only recently been reported by our group, showed no aldosterone binding and no transactivation because of a major change in receptor conformation.

findings.statement: Riepe et al. (2006) showed that the heterozygous NR3C2 missense mutation S818L found in a PHA1 patient did not bind aldosterone, activate transcription, or translocate into the nucleus; 3-dimensional modeling showed a major displacement of several residues involved in aldosterone binding.
quotes: S818L does not bind aldosterone or activate transcription or translocate into the nucleus. A major displacement of several residues involved in aldosterone binding was PHA1 causing.

findings.statement: Riepe et al. (2006) identified a novel heterozygous NR3C2 missense mutation, E972G, in a PHA1 patient; the mutant showed significantly lower ligand-binding affinity and only 9% of wildtype transcriptional activity, caused by major changes in receptor conformation.
quotes: The novel E972G mutation showed a significantly lower ligand-binding affinity and only 9% of wild-type transcriptional activity caused by major changes in receptor conformation.

relevance_reason: Only the title is available. It describes a salt-losing syndrome in infancy that the authors called pseudo-hypoadrenocorticalism, an early clinical description that fits pseudohypoaldosteronism type I. The title doesn't say how it was inherited, how many patients there were, or which genes were involved.

findings.statement: RAINE and ROY (1962) described a salt-losing syndrome in infancy, which they called pseudo-hypoadrenocorticalism.
quotes: A salt-losing syndrome in infancy. Pseudo-hypoadrenocorticalism.

relevance_reason: This is the classic early description of pseudohypoadrenocorticism: renal sodium loss with hyponatremia and hyperkalemia caused by renal tubular insensitivity to mineralocorticoids. Only the title was available.

findings.statement: DONNELL et al. (1959) described pseudohypo-adrenalocorticism, a condition marked by renal sodium loss, hyponatremia, and hyperkalemia. They attributed it to insensitivity of the renal tubules to mineralocorticoids.
quotes: Pseudohypo-adrenalocorticism; renal sodium loss, hyponatremia, and hyperkalemia due to a renal tubular insensitivity to mineralocorticoids.

relevance_reason: Only the title is available. It describes a salt-wasting syndrome in infancy, which matches the phenotype of this entry, but no details can be extracted.

findings.statement: CHEEK and PERRY (1958) reported a salt-wasting syndrome in infancy.
quotes: A salt wasting syndrome in infancy.

relevance_reason: Reports NR3C2 (hMR) mutations and functional studies in 14 families with autosomal dominant or sporadic PHA1.

findings.statement: Sartorato et al. (2003) analyzed the mineralocorticoid receptor (hMR) gene in 14 families with autosomal dominant or sporadic PHA1, which is characterized by neonatal renal salt wasting and failure to thrive, and found 6 different heterozygous mutations. The authors concluded that hMR mutations are a common feature of autosomal dominant PHA1, since they were found in 70% of their familial cases.
quotes: We have analyzed the human mineralocorticoid receptor (hMR) gene in 14 families with autosomal dominant or sporadic pseudohypoaldosteronism (PHA1), a rare form of mineralocorticoid resistance characterized by neonatal renal salt wasting and failure to thrive. Six heterozygous mutations were detected.
We conclude that hMR mutations are a common feature of autosomal dominant PHA1, being found in 70% of our familial cases.

findings.statement: In PHA1 families, Sartorato et al. (2003) found a heterozygous frameshift mutation in exon 2 of the hMR gene (insT1354). It is predicted to produce a truncated protein because of a premature stop codon.
quotes: Two frameshift mutations in exon 2 (insT1354, del8bp537) and one nonsense mutation in exon 4 (C2157A, Cys645stop) generate truncated proteins due to premature stop codons.

findings.statement: In PHA1 families, Sartorato et al. (2003) found a heterozygous 8-bp deletion in exon 2 of the hMR gene (del8bp537). It causes a frameshift and is predicted to produce a truncated protein because of a premature stop codon.
quotes: Two frameshift mutations in exon 2 (insT1354, del8bp537) and one nonsense mutation in exon 4 (C2157A, Cys645stop) generate truncated proteins due to premature stop codons.

findings.statement: In PHA1 families, Sartorato et al. (2003) found a heterozygous nonsense mutation in exon 4 of the hMR gene, C2157A, which changes cys645 to a stop codon (Cys645stop). It is predicted to produce a truncated protein.
quotes: Two frameshift mutations in exon 2 (insT1354, del8bp537) and one nonsense mutation in exon 4 (C2157A, Cys645stop) generate truncated proteins due to premature stop codons.

findings.statement: In PHA1, Sartorato et al. (2003) found a heterozygous G633R missense mutation in the DNA-binding domain of hMR. The R633 mutant had reduced maximal transactivation, but its binding characteristics and ED50 of transactivation were comparable to wildtype hMR. The authors suggested that the mutation probably causes haploinsufficiency.
quotes: The DNA binding domain mutant R633 exhibits reduced maximal transactivation, although its binding characteristics and ED(50) of transactivation are comparable with wild-type hMR.
whereas mutations G633R and Q776R probably result in haploinsufficiency in PHA1 patients

findings.statement: In PHA1, Sartorato et al. (2003) found a heterozygous Q776R missense mutation in the ligand-binding domain of hMR. The R776 mutant had reduced aldosterone binding and reduced ligand-dependent transactivation. The authors suggested that the mutation probably causes haploinsufficiency.
quotes: Ligand binding domain mutants R776 and P979 present reduced or absent aldosterone binding, respectively, which is associated with reduced or absent ligand-dependent transactivation capacity.
whereas mutations G633R and Q776R probably result in haploinsufficiency in PHA1 patients

findings.statement: In PHA1, Sartorato et al. (2003) found a heterozygous L979P missense mutation in the ligand-binding domain of hMR. The P979 mutant did not bind aldosterone, had no ligand-dependent transactivation, and had a transdominant negative effect on wildtype hMR activity.
quotes: Ligand binding domain mutants R776 and P979 present reduced or absent aldosterone binding, respectively, which is associated with reduced or absent ligand-dependent transactivation capacity.
Finally, P979 possesses a transdominant negative effect on wild-type hMR activity

findings.statement: Sartorato et al. (2003) did not find hMR mutations in some families with PHA1. They noted that this points to the need for extensive investigation of the hMR gene and to other genes possibly involved in the disease.
quotes: Their absence in some families underscores the importance of an extensive investigation of the hMR gene and the role of precise diagnostic procedures to allow for identification of other genes potentially involved in the disease.

relevance_reason: The paper reports a new NR3C2 (hMR) frameshift mutation in a sporadic case of PHA1 and finds no hMR mutations in two autosomal dominant kindreds, which is evidence for genetic heterogeneity.

findings.statement: In a patient with sporadic pseudohypoaldosteronism type I, Viemann et al. (2001) identified a frameshift mutation, Ins2871C, in exon 9 of the mineralocorticoid receptor gene (hMR). The mutation was not found in the patient's asymptomatic family members. It was the first mutation described in exon 9 and affects the last 27 amino acids of the hormone-binding domain.
quotes: In the sporadic case we identified a new frameshift mutation, Ins2871C, in exon 9 of the hMR gene. Family members were asymptomatic and had no mutation.
This mutation is the first described in exon 9 and impairs the last 27 amino acids of the hormone-binding domain.

phenotypes.text: neonatal salt wasting resistant to mineralocorticoids

findings.statement: Viemann et al. (2001) found no mutation in the hMR gene in 5 affected patients from 2 families with autosomal dominant PHA I. They concluded that autosomal dominant or sporadic PHA1 is genetically heterogeneous and involves other, as yet unidentified, genes.
quotes: In 2 kindreds with autosomal dominant PHA1 we found no mutation of the hMR gene.
Our results confirm the hypothesis that autosomal dominant or sporadic PHA1 is a genetically heterogeneous disease involving other, as yet unidentified, genes.

relevance_reason: Reports a novel NR3C2 (MR) missense mutation with functional loss in a Japanese family with autosomal dominant renal PHA1.

findings.statement: In affected members of a Japanese family with a renal form of PHA1, Tajima et al. (2000) identified by PCR and direct sequencing a heterozygous point mutation in the mineralocorticoid receptor (MR) gene changing codon 924 from leu (CTG) to pro (CCG) (L924P). In COS-1 cells transfected with a GRE-tk-CAT reporter, aldosterone increased CAT activity with wildtype receptor but had no effect with the L924P mutant. The authors suggested that mineralocorticoid resistance in this family was due to the missense mutation, the first missense MR mutation reported in renal PHA1.
quotes: PCR and direct sequencing of the MR gene identified a heterozygous point mutation changing codon 924 Leu (CTG) to CCG (Pro) (L924P) in all affected members.
Aldosterone increased CAT activity in cells expressing wild-type receptor, but had no effect in cells expressing the mutant receptors.
These results suggest that mineralocorticoid resistance in this family is due to a missense mutation in the MR gene.

findings.statement: Tajima et al. (2000) noted that PHA1 is characterized by neonatal salt loss with dehydration, hypotension, hyperkalemia, and metabolic acidosis despite elevated plasma aldosterone and PRA; the autosomal dominant form manifests milder salt wasting that gradually improves with age, in contrast to the severe multiorgan autosomal recessive form.
quotes: Pseudohypoaldosteronism type 1 (PHA1) is a rare condition characterized by neonatal salt loss with dehydration, hypotension, hyperkalemia, and metabolic acidosis, despite elevated plasma aldosterone levels and PRA.
Contrary, an autosomal dominant PHA1 manifests milder salt wasting that gradually improves with advancing age.

relevance_reason: The paper identifies heterozygous mineralocorticoid receptor (MLR/NR3C2) mutations as the cause of autosomal dominant/sporadic PHA1.

findings.statement: Geller et al. (1998) described pseudohypoaldosteronism type I (PHA1) as neonatal renal salt wasting with dehydration, hypotension, hyperkalemia and metabolic acidosis, even though aldosterone levels are high. They contrasted the severe autosomal recessive form, which persists into adulthood and is caused by ENaC loss-of-function mutations, with the autosomal dominant or sporadic form, which is milder and remits with age.
quotes: Pseudohypoaldosteronism type I (PHA1) is characterized by neonatal renal salt wasting with dehydration, hypotension, hyperkalaemia and metabolic acidosis, despite elevated aldosterone levels.
Autosomal dominant or sporadic PHA1 is a milder disease that remits with age.

findings.statement: Geller et al. (1998) found no ENaC gene mutations in 6 dominant and 7 sporadic PHA1 kindreds, which pointed to mutations in other genes in the dominant form.
quotes: Among six dominant and seven sporadic PHA1 kindreds, we have found no ENaC gene mutations, implicating mutations in other genes.

findings.statement: Geller et al. (1998) screened the mineralocorticoid receptor gene (MLR) in 13 dominant or sporadic PHA1 kindreds. They found heterozygous mutations in 1 sporadic and 4 dominant kindreds: 2 frameshift mutations (1 of them de novo), 2 premature termination codons and 1 splice donor mutation. The mutations segregated with PHA1 and were absent from unaffected subjects. The authors concluded that heterozygous MLR mutations cause PHA1.
quotes: we have screened the mineralocorticoid receptor gene (MLR) for variants and have identified heterozygous mutations in one sporadic and four dominant kindreds.
These include two frameshift mutations (one a de novo mutation), two premature termination codons and one splice donor mutation.
These mutations segregate with PHA1 and are not found in unaffected subjects.

relevance_reason: Reports three patients with pseudohypoaldosteronism and shows absent or reduced aldosterone (Type I) receptor binding in their mononuclear leukocytes. This is early evidence for a mineralocorticoid receptor defect. The authors suggest autosomal recessive transmission in one consanguineous family.

findings.statement: Armanini et al. (1985) studied 3 patients with pseudohypoaldosteronism. These were a 28-year-old index case from Melbourne and 2 siblings from Munich, aged 8 and 2 years, whose parents were first cousins. The younger sibling, a boy, was less severely affected than his sister. The authors described the syndrome as salt wasting and failure to thrive, usually presenting in infancy with high urinary sodium despite hyponatremia, together with hyperkalemia, hyperreninemia, and elevated aldosterone levels.
quotes: Pseudohypoaldosteronism, a syndrome characterized by salt wasting and failure to thrive, usually presents in infancy as high urinary levels of sodium despite hyponatremia, hyperkalemia, hyperreninemia, and elevated aldosterone levels.

We have studied three patients with pseudohypoaldosteronism: the 28-year-old index case in Melbourne (Patient 1) and two siblings in Munich, eight and two years of age (Patients 2 and 3); clinically, Patient 3 had a less severe case than his sister.

findings.statement: Armanini et al. (1985) found that Percoll-separated monocytes from controls bound [3H]aldosterone with high affinity (Kd about 3 nM) and limited capacity (150 to 600 sites per cell). On repeated testing, no [3H]aldosterone binding was found in monocytes from patients 1 and 2. Patient 3, who was less severely affected, had 62 sites per cell, more than 2 SD below the control level. The parents of the Munich siblings had normal levels. The authors concluded that pseudohypoaldosteronism is caused by a Type I (mineralocorticoid) receptor defect that may be complete or partial.
quotes: Percoll-separated control monocytes bound [3H]aldosterone with high affinity (Kd approximately 3 nM) and limited capacity (150 to 600 sites per cell).
On repeated examination, no [3H]aldosterone binding was found in monocytes from Patients 1 and 2; in Patient 3, the levels were 62 sites per cell, more than 2 S.D. below those of the control.
It appears that pseudohypoaldosteronism is caused by a Type I receptor defect, that the defect may be complete or partial

phenotypes.text: absent or reduced aldosterone binding in mononuclear leukocytes

findings.statement: In the Munich family, the parents were first cousins and had normal monocyte aldosterone-receptor levels. Armanini et al. (1985) suggested that transmission of pseudohypoaldosteronism may be autosomal recessive.
quotes: Levels in the parents of the Munich patients (first cousins) were normal.
that transmission may be autosomal recessive

relevance_reason: Clinical description of a kindred with renal PHA I showing autosomal dominant transmission, and distinction from autosomal recessive multiple-organ form.

findings.statement: Hanukoglu (1991) described a kindred (kindred I) with type I pseudohypoaldosteronism in which the propositus presented in infancy with renal salt wasting, including vomiting, failure to thrive, short stature, hyponatremia, and hyperkalemia, and responded dramatically to a high salt diet (2.5 g/day); sodium supplementation was discontinued at age 2 years. In 7 additional family members from 3 generations, clinical expression varied from asymptomatic to moderate.
quotes: In kindred I, the propositus presented with renal salt wasting in infancy (vomiting, failure to thrive, short stature, hyponatremia, hyperkalemia) and responded dramatically to a high salt diet (2.5 g/day). Sodium supplementation was discontinued at the age of two.
In seven additional family members from three generations, clinical expression of PHA varied from asymptomatic to moderate.

findings.statement: In affected members of kindred I (propositus, mother, and 2 brothers), Hanukoglu (1991) found that hyperaldosteronism persisted over 13 years while plasma renin activity decreased gradually to near-normal values, which was interpreted as development of tertiary hyperaldosteronism due to an autonomously functioning zona glomerulosa.
quotes: In affected members (propositus, mother, and two brothers), hyperaldosteronism persisted over 13 yr; however, the PRA decreased gradually to near normal values.
Persistent hyperaldosteronism in the face of a decrease in PRA indicated the development of tertiary hyperaldosteronism due to autonomously functioning zona glomerulosa.

phenotypes.text: elevated plasma renin activity decreasing to near normal

findings.statement: Hanukoglu (1991) concluded that the pedigree of kindred I, with renal PHA I, was consistent with autosomal dominant transmission with variable expression.
quotes: The pedigree was consistent with an autosomal dominant mode of transmission with variable expression.

findings.statement: Hanukoglu (1991) described a second kindred in which the propositus, the offspring of a consanguineous marriage, developed severe renal salt losing at age 9 days with increased salivary and sweat electrolytes, indicating multiple target organ unresponsiveness to mineralocorticoids; life-threatening salt wasting recurred beyond age 2, and at 5 years she required 14 g/day salt. A sister died at 9 days with PHA symptoms, and the pedigree was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance. From these kindreds and the literature, the author concluded that type I PHA comprises 2 clinically and genetically distinct entities with either renal or multiple target organ defects.
quotes: In kindred II, the propositus, who was the product of a consanguineous marriage, developed severe renal salt losing at age 9 days.
She had also increased salivary and sweat electrolytes consistent with PHA resulting from multiple organ unresponsiveness to mineralocorticoids.
we conclude that type I PHA includes two clinically and genetically distinct entities with either renal or multiple target organ defects.

relevance_reason: Only the title, 'Inheritance of pseudohypoaldosteronism', is available. It shows the paper is about how pseudohypoaldosteronism is inherited, which is relevant to this autosomal dominant PHA1 entry. However, it gives no inheritance mode, patients, families or variants, so no findings can be backed by quotes.
